sport.title: November 20, 1988: The day Gabriela Sabatini won her first big title
paras: On 20 November 1988, 18‑year‑old Gabriela Sabatini beat Pam Shriver in Madison Square Garden, winning the Virginia Slims Championships. This match gave Gabriela her first major title and made her top‑ten world No. 4, proving she could beat the best players, like Steffi Graf and Martina Navratilova, on big stages.

Gabriela had already reached three big finals before 1988, but nobody had stopped her until this victory. Pam Shriver, a powerful American player, had won 23 tournament titles and was world No. 3, so defeating her showed Gabriela’s skill and confidence. The win also marked the first time an Argentinewoman claimed a top‑level title in the United States, inspiring countless young players.

sport.title: Doha and Dubai’s future, a 2028 calendar shake-up, clay to hard: what’s on the table as Gaudenzi speaks in Tur
paras: Replacement options for the two Gulf 500s, Acapulco’s exit in 2028, Rotterdam moving to the autumn and several clay events eyeing hard courts: the files reportedly on the ATP’s table in Turin.

Whether Doha and Dubai will be played in February 2027 is the first question on the table as ATP Chairman Andrea Gaudenzi holds his press conference in Turin on Friday. According to Ercoli, the ATP has given itself December 1 as the ideal date to decide on 2027, and the uncertainty comes from the Gulf situation, still unstable.

sport.title: Five players David Ferrer could call upon to replace Carlos Alcaraz if he withdraws from Davis Cup Finals with
paras: After requiring treatment against Daniil Medvedev at the ATP Finals, Alcaraz underwent an MRI . He has been cleared to continue in Turin, but whether he will be fit to complete the tournament and then play the Davis Cup Finals next week remains to be seen.

Spain’s Davis Cup captain, David Ferrer, said he needs Alcaraz to win the title , but what happens if they lose their star man? Here are five players Ferrer could call upon to replace him for the trip to Bologna. Spanish veteran Pablo Carreno Busta would be a solid replacement for Alcaraz.
